production.note: US model years 1999-2005 (Consumer Guide's used-car review of the 1999-05 Miata, Tom Appel). Mazda's US brochure 'MAZDA FOR 2005' still lists the car (mazda-us-2005-mx5-brochure); the next-generation NC was a 2006 model. This record is the 1.8 naturally aspirated car; the turbocharged Mazdaspeed MX-5 (2004-2005) is a separate variant.

body.note: '2-door convertible'; a two-seat open car with no fixed-roof version, so Roadster under the data guide

configuration.note: 'Engine size and type 1.8L 4-cylinder; iron block with light-alloy cylinder head'

displacementL.note: '1.8L'. No opened page gives the cc figure.

aspiration.note: Consumer Guide describes the standard 'dual-overhead-cam, 1.8-liter 4-cylinder engine' and lists the 'turbocharged' engine only for the separate MazdaSpeed model

transmission.note: Curb weight row lists '5-speed /6-speed /automatic'. Consumer Guide: 'A five-speed manual transmission was standard, with 4-speed automatic optional. A 6-speed manual gearbox could go into the LS edition.' Mazda's 2003 brochure: '4-speed automatic overdrive transmission' (mazda-us-2003-mx5-brochure).

powerHp.note: 2002 model year. Quote: "Horsepower, SAE Net 142 @ 7000 rpm". Same in the 2003 brochure ("142 @ 7000 rpm", mazda-us-2003-mx5-brochure) and the 2005 brochure ("Horsepower, SAE Net" "142 @ 7000 rpm", mazda-us-2005-mx5-brochure). 142 hp applied to the 2001-2005 cars, five of the seven model years; the 1999-2000 cars were rated 140 hp. Consumer Guide: "Mazda's dual-overhead-cam, 1.8-liter 4-cylinder engine produced 140 horsepower until 2001, when it got a boost to 142–not 155, as early announcements stated." Mazda originally advertised the 2001 car at 155 hp and later corrected it (The Auto Channel, 2001: "Mazda said it overstated the horsepower of the 2001 model...by about 8 percent", theautochannel-2001-miata-hp), which is why 2002, not 2001, is the reference year.

weightLb.note: Base car with the standard 5-speed manual, 2002 model year. Quote: "Curb weight (5-speed /6-speed /automatic) 2387/ 2447/ 2429 lb". Later Mazda brochures give heavier 5-speed figures: 2003 "2443/2454/2485 lb" (mazda-us-2003-mx5-brochure), 2005 "Curb weight (5-speed/6-speed/automatic)" "2447/2441/2474 lb" (mazda-us-2005-mx5-brochure). No 2001 Mazda brochure or release was opened.

discrepancies.reason: Model year. All are Mazda US curb weights for the 5-speed manual car: 2,387 lb (2002), 2,443 lb (2003), 2,447 lb (2005).
discrepancies.resolution: Used 2,387 lb because the reference model year is 2002, the earliest 142 hp year with a Mazda curb weight found.

discrepancies.reason: Model year. 140 hp for 1999-2000, 142 hp for 2001-2005 (the 2001 car was first announced at 155 hp, later corrected to 142).
discrepancies.resolution: Used 142 hp, the rating for five of the seven model years.
